knowledge:
- key_parameters: ld.threshold=The threshold for linkage disequilibrium pruning (e.g., 0.2) ;; method=In snpgdsVCF2GDS, specifies whether to extract "biallelic.only" or all variant sites ;; num.thread=The number of CPU cores/threads to use for parallel computing in PCA, IBD, and IBS calculations ;; maf=Minor allele frequency threshold used to filter SNPs in relatedness analyses ;; missing.rate=Missing rate threshold used to filter SNPs in relatedness analyses ;; snpfirstdim=Logical parameter in snpgdsCreateGeno indicating if the first dimension of the genotype matrix represents SNPs
- alternatives: SeqArray=Strongly suggested instead of SNPRelate for large-scale whole-exome and whole-genome sequencing variant data (using seqVCF2GDS and seqGetData) ;; GWASTools=An R/Bioconductor package that also uses the GDS format and provides extensive quality control and association testing functions
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing large-scale GWAS SNP data to perform population structure identification (PCA), relatedness estimation (IBD/kinship), Fst estimation, or sample clustering on multi-core systems.
- pitfalls: Strong linkage disequilibrium (LD) among SNPs can heavily bias PCA and relatedness analyses, making LD-based SNP pruning a critical prerequisite ;; The variables snp.position and snp.chromosome in the GDS file do not allow NA values ;; Offspring should be removed from the dataset when estimating Fst across multiple populations to avoid bias ;; SNPRelate is optimized for bi-allelic SNP data; for multi-allelic sequencing data, SeqArray should be used instead.

workflows.name: gds_format_conversion
workflows.intent: Convert PLINK binary files or VCF files into the GDS format required for downstream SNPRelate analyses.
workflows.stages: 1. Convert PLINK BED/FAM/BIM files to GDS using snpgdsBED2GDS ;; 2. Convert VCF files to GDS using snpgdsVCF2GDS ;; 3. Summarize the converted GDS file using snpgdsSummary.
workflows.code:
# Convert PLINK
snpgdsBED2GDS(bed.fn, fam.fn, bim.fn, "test.gds")

# Summary
snpgdsSummary("test.gds")

# Convert VCF
snpgdsVCF2GDS(vcf.fn, "test.gds", method="biallelic.only")

# Summary
snpgdsSummary("test.gds")

workflows.name: pca_and_population_structure
workflows.intent: Perform LD-based SNP pruning and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to identify population structure and calculate SNP-PC correlations.
workflows.stages: 1. Open GDS file using snpgdsOpen ;; 2. Perform LD-based SNP pruning using snpgdsLDpruning ;; 3. Extract pruned SNP IDs ;; 4. Run PCA using snpgdsPCA ;; 5. Calculate PC-correlated SNPs using snpgdsPCACorr ;; 6. Close GDS file using snpgdsClose.
workflows.code:
# Open the GDS file
genofile <- snpgdsOpen(snpgdsExampleFileName())

set.seed(1000)

# Try different LD thresholds for sensitivity analysis
snpset <- snpgdsLDpruning(genofile, ld.threshold=0.2)

# Get all selected snp id
snpset.id <- unlist(unname(snpset))

# Run PCA
pca <- snpgdsPCA(genofile, snp.id=snpset.id, num.thread=2)

# variance proportion (%)
pc.percent <- pca$varprop*100
head(round(pc.percent, 2))

# make a data.frame
tab <- data.frame(sample.id = pca$sample.id,
    EV1 = pca$eigenvect[,1],    # the first eigenvector
    EV2 = pca$eigenvect[,2],    # the second eigenvector
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Draw
plot(tab$EV2, tab$EV1, xlab="eigenvector 2", ylab="eigenvector 1")

# Get chromosome index
chr <- read.gdsn(index.gdsn(genofile, "snp.chromosome"))
CORR <- snpgdsPCACorr(pca, genofile, eig.which=1:4)

# Close the GDS file
snpgdsClose(genofile)

workflows.name: relatedness_and_relationship_inference
workflows.intent: Estimate identity-by-descent (IBD) coefficients and kinship using PLINK Method of Moments, Maximum Likelihood Estimation, or KING robust method.
workflows.stages: 1. Open GDS file using snpgdsOpen ;; 2. Perform IBD estimation via Method of Moments using snpgdsIBDMoM ;; 3. Perform IBD estimation via Maximum Likelihood Estimation using snpgdsIBDMLE ;; 4. Infer relationships using the KING robust method with snpgdsIBDKING ;; 5. Select and format IBD/kinship coefficients using snpgdsIBDSelection ;; 6. Close GDS file using snpgdsClose.
workflows.code:
# Open the GDS file
genofile <- snpgdsOpen(snpgdsExampleFileName())

# Get population information
pop_code <- read.gdsn(index.gdsn(genofile, path="sample.annot/pop.group"))

# YRI samples
sample.id <- read.gdsn(index.gdsn(genofile, "sample.id"))
YRI.id <- sample.id[pop_code == "YRI"]

# Estimate IBD coefficients using MoM
ibd <- snpgdsIBDMoM(genofile, sample.id=YRI.id, snp.id=snpset.id,
    maf=0.05, missing.rate=0.05, num.thread=2)

# Make a data.frame
ibd.coeff <- snpgdsIBDSelection(ibd)

# Estimate IBD coefficients using MLE
set.seed(100)
snp.id <- sample(snpset.id, 1500)  # random 1500 SNPs
ibd <- snpgdsIBDMLE(genofile, sample.id=YRI.id, snp.id=snp.id,
    maf=0.05, missing.rate=0.05, num.thread=2)

# Make a data.frame
ibd.coeff <- snpgdsIBDSelection(ibd)

# Incorporate with pedigree information
family.id <- read.gdsn(index.gdsn(genofile, "sample.annot/family.id"))
family.id <- family.id[match(YRI.id, sample.id)]

ibd.robust <- snpgdsIBDKING(genofile, sample.id=YRI.id,
    family.id=family.id, num.thread=2)

# Pairs of individuals
dat <- snpgdsIBDSelection(ibd.robust)

# Close the GDS file
snpgdsClose(genofile)

workflows.name: ibs_and_cluster_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform Identity-By-State (IBS) analysis, multidimensional scaling (MDS), and hierarchical clustering to group individuals.
workflows.stages: 1. Open GDS file using snpgdsOpen ;; 2. Calculate average IBS pairwise identities using snpgdsIBS ;; 3. Perform multidimensional scaling using cmdscale ;; 4. Perform hierarchical clustering using snpgdsHCluster ;; 5. Determine clusters of individuals using snpgdsCutTree ;; 6. Close GDS file using snpgdsClose.
workflows.code:
# Open the GDS file
genofile <- snpgdsOpen(snpgdsExampleFileName())

# Get population information
pop_code <- read.gdsn(index.gdsn(genofile, path="sample.annot/pop.group"))

ibs <- snpgdsIBS(genofile, num.thread=2)

# individuals in the same population are clustered together
pop.idx <- order(pop_code)
image(ibs$ibs[pop.idx, pop.idx], col=terrain.colors(16))

loc <- cmdscale(1 - ibs$ibs, k = 2)
x <- loc[, 1]; y <- loc[, 2]
race <- as.factor(pop_code)

set.seed(100)
ibs.hc <- snpgdsHCluster(snpgdsIBS(genofile, num.thread=2))

# Determine groups of individuals automatically
rv <- snpgdsCutTree(ibs.hc)

# Determine groups of individuals by population information
rv2 <- snpgdsCutTree(ibs.hc, samp.group=as.factor(pop_code))

# Close the GDS file
snpgdsClose(genofile)
